paper.title_en: Probing Dirac Heavy Neutral Leptons through EFT-Induced Meson Decays
paper.abstract_en: We investigate dimension-six operators involving pairs of Dirac-type heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) at beam-dump and far-forward experiments. In the $ν$SMEFT framework, lepton-number-conserving four-fermion operators couple HNL pairs to quarks and induce two and three-body charm and bottom meson decays. We study the $c\to u$, $b\to d$, and $b\to s$ transitions at FASER2, FACET, SHiP, and two FPF@FCC configurations. HNL production depends on the cut-off scale $Λ$, while the lifetime depends on the active-sterile mixing $|V_{eN}|^2$. Sizable production can therefore coexist with the small mixing needed for HNLs to reach distant detectors. We project sensitivities in the $(M_N,|V_{eN}|^2)$ and $(M_N,Λ)$ planes, accounting for two and three-body decays and constraints from invisible and semivisible meson decays. SHiP is particularly sensitive to $c\to u$, while the larger FCC-LLP2 configuration probes $b\to d, s$. We find that EFT-induced pair production extends long-lived HNL searches to very small mixing and complements other probes of the $ν$SMEFT heavy-neutrino sector.
